faqs.q: Will AI replace full stack developers?
faqs.a: AI is unlikely to replace full stack developers; it mainly speeds up their work. AI tools can generate code for routine tasks, but someone still has to design the system, connect the frontend, backend, database and cloud, check the output and understand the business needs behind the product.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a full stack developer and a frontend or backend developer?
faqs.a: A frontend developer builds what users see and interact with, and a backend developer builds the servers, APIs and databases behind it. A full stack developer can work on both, and usually also handles authentication, deployment and how all the parts of an application fit together.

faqs.q: What skills do I need to become a full stack developer in the AI era?
faqs.a: Core skills include JavaScript, a frontend framework such as React, a backend runtime such as Node.js, databases, APIs and cloud deployment. On top of these, it helps to learn how to connect an application to AI models through APIs and how to review AI-generated code critically.

faqs.q: Is full stack development still a good career choice for freshers?
faqs.a: It remains a useful skill set because many companies, especially startups, prefer engineers who can work across several parts of a product. AI has raised expectations rather than removed the need for developers, so freshers who understand complete systems and can use AI tools well are better placed than those who only know one framework.
